requirements.invariant: Accept only the verified canonical nonempty ClearItemSpaceAssignmentsCommand bound to the runtime Account/Principal and preserve its opaque stable OperationID. Project and Business Inventory are distinct exact scopes; one clear may contain Items from different current Spaces in that scope.

One transaction persists one canonical localOnly clearing-command row and one generic queued local operation. `spike_item_space_clearing_commands` uses operation ID as implicit text `id`; required text `account_id`, `actor_principal_id`, `contract_version`, `scope_kind`, `items_json`, `fingerprint`, `command_json`; nullable text `project_id`; required integer `accepted_at_ms`; and index `item_space_clearing_command_account` on `account_id`. It produces no ps_crud and writes no Item, Space, or marker projection.

Persist and revalidate byte-identical canonical command/envelope JSON, fingerprint, scope, Project-or-Account subject, stable Item order, every current Space, and every Item revision as canonical UInt64 decimal text. `items_json` is sorted-key canonical JSON `{schemaVersion:"item_space_clearing_items_v1",items:[{itemId,expectedRevision,currentSpaceId}]}`. Generic `subject_id` is the Project or Account, command type is `clear_item_space_assignments`, and `command_expected_revision` is null. The canonical JSON, not decoded-Date equality or an integer derivative, owns every finite command-valid client time. Provider acceptance time is consulted only after replay lookup for new admission, truncates toward zero, and must be finite, nonnegative, within Int64, and exactly round-trip through the public Date snapshot; malformed persisted acceptance time fails symmetrically.

Exact replay returns the existing queued receipt only after all clearing and generic-operation evidence matches. Changed replay uses OperationContractFailure.payloadMismatch; Account/Principal mismatch uses existing runtime scope failures; malformed, orphaned, terminal, result-bearing, or cross-family OperationID evidence fails closed without repair. The provider registers its command type and local command table once in the separately verified centralized guard, so complete, orphaned, malformed, and concurrent collisions against every existing family fail closed in both directions without pairwise store coupling. Concurrent same-family calls converge on one durable outcome.

Cancellation before commit leaves no evidence; cancellation after atomic commit cannot revoke accepted work. Non-destructive encrypted close/reopen retains both rows. This slice exposes no deletion, repair, terminal transition, or upload API; later session-ending and reconciliation policy owns removal.

LedgerOfflineClientRuntime nominally satisfies ItemSpaceAssignmentClearing and is directly consumable by ItemSpaceClearingUseCase. Normal bootstrap constructs and binds exactly one clearing store on the structured Account database. Expose one finite clearing submission and one clearing-specific OperationID watch through the existing lifecycle owner/facade. The watch scopes by exact opaque ID plus constructor Account/Principal, emits only fully validated queued evidence, and invents no applying or terminal semantics. Cancellation and close join all provider/runtime watches and admitted operations before structured database close; post-close admission refuses before database access.
The existing pending-work summary counts the accepted clear exactly once through its generic queued operation and does not infer upload or remote durability.

No authoritative placement or marker cleanup, optimistic projection, upload connector, Postgres/RLS/Data API/Sync Stream/RPC, capability decision, app/MCP, hosted, Firebase, migration, production, or cutover behavior advances. O-037 archive effects and O-023 attachment-reference/byte deletion remain unresolved. Raw persistence/watch failures map to localAcceptanceFailed without partial mutation or emission; CancellationError remains control flow.
